reasons: Some response fields are read without checks, so an unexpected reply can break the panel.
Several response types are loose (any), and the code itself notes an open task to type them.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and helper setup
sections.what: Brings in React tools, icons, and the overs and run rate helpers from the engine folder.
sections.why: Likely reason: the cricket arithmetic lives in one shared place so every screen agrees.
sections.watch_out: Renaming these helpers breaks the score maths in this panel.

sections.name: rateOf, formatRate
sections.title: Run rate display helpers
sections.what: Turns runs and overs text into a run rate and a two-decimal text. If the overs text cannot be read, it shows a dash.
sections.why: The comment says overs such as 10.4 mean ten overs and four balls, not a decimal number.
sections.watch_out: Treating overs as decimal numbers gives wrong run rates.

sections.name: ScoreEntry
sections.title: Score row shape
sections.what: Describes one innings score: runs, wickets, overs text, and the innings label.
sections.why: Describes the server data so the code knows which fields exist.
sections.watch_out: Team names are cut out of the innings label by text matching, so a label change changes what is shown.

sections.name: TeamData
sections.title: Team shape
sections.what: Describes a team with a full name, a short name and an optional image.
sections.why: Describes the team data sent by the server.
sections.watch_out: The image field is declared but not used in the visible lines.

sections.name: InningsData
sections.title: Innings detail shape
sections.what: Describes full innings data: totals, extras, batsmen, bowlers, fall of wickets and partnerships.
sections.why: The comment calls this a legacy untyped payload to be replaced later.
sections.watch_out: Batsmen, bowlers and the related lists are untyped, so their contents are not checked.

sections.name: MatchData
sections.title: Match shape
sections.what: Describes one match: name, status, scores, teams, target, venue, date, toss and result.
sections.why: Describes the server match data so the screen knows what to show.
sections.watch_out: If the server renames or drops a field, the matching text goes blank or the panel breaks.

sections.name: APIResponse, TabKey
sections.title: Whole reply shape and tab names
sections.what: Describes the full reply: the primary match, the IPL matches, all other matches, and API usage. Also lists the four valid tab names.
sections.why: Describes the server reply and fixes the allowed tab choices.
sections.watch_out: The all-matches list is untyped, so the code trusts its shape.

sections.name: LiveMatchCenter (part 1)
sections.title: Component start, data loading and refresh timer
sections.what: Sets up memory for data, tab, auto refresh, loading, errors and selected match. Fetches scores on load and then every 30 seconds while auto refresh is on. The compact prop is accepted but no visible code reads it.
sections.why: Likely reason: scores stay current without the visitor reloading the page.
sections.watch_out: Each refresh uses one of the daily API calls, so many visitors on auto refresh will use the budget quickly.

sections.name: LiveMatchCenter: if
sections.title: Error, no-match and selected match header
sections.what: Shows an error with a retry button if loading failed and nothing is on screen. Shows a no-match message if there is no primary match. Otherwise picks the chosen IPL match, falling back to the primary match, and draws the header with a live, result or upcoming label, the source, the auto toggle and a manual refresh button.
sections.why: Likely reason: the visitor always sees a clear state rather than a blank panel.
sections.watch_out: If the chosen index no longer exists in the list, the panel silently shows the primary match instead.

sections.name: LiveMatchCenter (part 3)
sections.title: Match name, innings scores and status
sections.what: Shows the match name, one line per innings with runs, wickets and overs, the status text, and the target for a live match.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a quick summary at the top of the panel.
sections.watch_out: The last innings is highlighted as active only while the match is live, so a finished match shows no active highlight.

sections.name: LiveMatchCenter (part 4)
sections.title: Match picker and tab bar
sections.what: When several IPL matches exist, shows buttons to switch between them. Also shows the four tab buttons with icons.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets visitors move between games and views without leaving the panel.
sections.watch_out: The tab labels are fixed English text and are not passed through the translation lookup.

sections.name: LiveMatchCenter (part 5)
sections.title: Live score tab
sections.what: For each innings, shows the team, runs and wickets, overs, run rate, and a bar showing progress through a 20-over innings. The bar turns colour above run rates of 10 and of 7.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a quick sense of the pace of play.
sections.watch_out: The bar scales against 120 balls, which is 20 overs, so other match lengths will show the wrong fill.

sections.name: LiveMatchCenter (part 6)
sections.title: Match status and usage line
sections.what: Shows the status card and a footnote saying the panel refreshes every 30 seconds and how many API calls were used today.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes the data limit visible to the visitor.
sections.watch_out: The usage line reads apiInfo directly, so a reply without that field will break this tab.

sections.name: LiveMatchCenter (part 7)
sections.title: Scorecard tab
sections.what: For each innings, shows team, runs, wickets, overs, run rate, ten wicket dots and twenty over blocks. The over blocks mark completed and current overs. Shows a waiting message if the match has not started.
sections.why: Likely reason: a quick visual summary of each innings.
sections.watch_out: The wicket dots and over blocks are fixed at ten and twenty, which suits only a standard 20-over innings.

sections.name: LiveMatchCenter (part 8)
sections.title: All matches tab
sections.what: Lists every IPL match with its status, score lines and venue. Tapping a match switches to the live tab showing that match.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a visitor choose a match from a list.
sections.watch_out: The heading contains fixed text for the 2026 season and will be wrong when the season changes.

sections.name: LiveMatchCenter (part 9)
sections.title: Other matches in progress
sections.what: Lists up to five matches that are not IPL, from the all-matches data, with name, score lines and status.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the heading text.
sections.watch_out: The filter depends on the match name containing the exact tournament name, and score fields are read loosely.

sections.name: LiveMatchCenter (part 10)
sections.title: Information tab and footer
sections.what: Shows a details table for the selected match: name, venue, date, toss, target, source, last updated time and result if any. Also shows a usage bar, an innings summary, and a footer with the source and update time.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets visitors judge how fresh the data is and where it came from.
sections.watch_out: The date is parsed directly, so a bad date value would show an invalid date text instead of an error.

summary: The main cricket score panel for IPL matches, with tabs for the live score, scorecard, all matches and match information.
purpose: Shows visitors the current IPL scores and match details, refreshing itself every 30 seconds.
why: The text 'We never show simulated scores as live' states a rule: only real scores are shown as live. Other reasons are not stated in the code.
how: 1. Fetches /api/live-score on load and every 30 seconds while auto refresh is on. 2. Keeps the response in memory. 3. Shows a loading message first, then an error with a retry button if nothing loaded, then a no-match message if there is no primary match. 4. Otherwise draws the header, the match picker, the tabs and the active tab, with scores, run rates, wicket dots and over progress.
inputs: The JSON reply from /api/live-score, the visitor's tab, match and auto refresh choices, and a compact prop that the visible code does not read.
outputs: A score panel with a footer that shows the data source and last update time.
risks: The panel expects specific fields in the reply. Some places read apiInfo without a check. Batsmen, bowlers and all-match data are loosely typed (any), so bad data may only fail at runtime. Refreshing every 30 seconds uses the daily request budget shown on screen.
debug: If the panel says no match but one is on, check the primary and iplMatches fields in the /api/live-score reply. If it stays on loading, check the network request. If numbers look wrong, check the run rate and overs parsing. If the usage counts show zero, check apiInfo in the reply.
